title: A Recipe for Disaster in Taiwan
author: Rebecca Lissner

A Recipe for Disaster in TaiwanWhy the Risk of a Crisis Is Growing Rebecca Lissner and Mira Rapp-Hooper November 9, 2026 An air defense drill in Taoyuan, Taiwan, August 2026 Cheng-Chia Huang / Reuters REBECCA LISSNER is Senior Fellow for U.S. Foreign Policy and Director of the Future of American Strategy Initiative at the Council on Foreign Relations. She served as Deputy Assistant to the President and Principal Deputy National Security Adviser to the Vice President during the Biden administration.MIRA RAPP-HOOPER is a Visiting Senior Fellow at the Brookings Institution. She was Special Assistant to the President and Senior Director for East Asia and Oceania and Director for Indo-Pacific Strategy at the U.S. National Security Council during the Biden administration. Request reprint permissions here.Just a few years ago, U.S. President Joe Biden caused a stir when he confirmed publicly that his administration would defend Taiwan if the island were attacked by China—a divergence from the traditional U.S. policy of strategic ambiguity, in which Washington does not commit to taking any particular action. In May, U.S. President Donald Trump made waves for taking a different position.
